commit.message:
lnwire: fix NodeAnnouncement2 address aliasing

The address decoders declared their scratch arrays outside the address
loop, so every decoded net.TCPAddr held a slice over the same backing
array. Each pass overwrote the addresses already appended, and the list
collapsed onto the last address read.

A message carrying 1.2.3.4:8080 and 5.6.7.8:8081 decoded as
5.6.7.8:8080 and 5.6.7.8:8081. The first address was lost. IPv6
behaved the same way. Tor v3 was immune because EncodeToString copies
the bytes into a string. We fix this by allocating within the address
loop iteration, even for tor to be consistent.

We update rapid tests to include several addresses.

lnwire: fix NodeAnnouncement2 short reads

The io.Reader contract lets a reader return fewer bytes than the caller
asked for with a nil error. The IPv4, IPv6 and Tor v3 address decoders
called Read for their fixed width fields and ignored the returned count,
so the untouched zero bytes of the scratch array became address data.

A 5 byte frame that declares a 6 byte IPv4 record decoded as
1.2.3.4:7936 with no error. io.ReadFull makes the short read an
io.ErrUnexpectedEOF.

The TLV format does not change and no complete valid record is rejected.

commit.message: docs: add release notes for migrate driver fix

sqldb/v2: close the Postgres migrate driver after use

The sqldb/v2 Postgres store has the same leak as sqldb. The pgx migrate
driver takes one connection from the pool it gets, and it keeps that
connection until the driver is closed. executeMigrations,
GetSchemaVersion and SetSchemaVersion used the shared pool and never
closed the driver, so each call held one connection for the life of the
store.

Each driver now gets its own database handle from the same DSN, and the
caller closes the driver. Closing the driver closes that handle and
leaves the shared pool open. A failed close is logged.

TestPostgresMigrateDriverReleasesConns is the same test as in sqldb.

sqldb: close the Postgres migrate driver after use

The pgx migrate driver takes one connection from the pool it gets, and
it keeps that connection until the driver is closed. ExecuteMigrations,
GetSchemaVersion and SetSchemaVersion used the shared pool and never
closed the driver. Each schema migration therefore held one connection
for the life of the store.

A fresh database runs 18 schema migration steps plus one schema version
read, so the store keeps 19 connections after startup. With the default
pool of 25, only 6 connections stay free. If db.postgres.maxconnections
is lower than 20, the migrations wait forever for a free connection,
and lnd does not start.

Each driver now gets its own database handle from the same DSN, and
the caller closes the driver. Closing the driver closes that handle and
leaves the shared pool open. A failed close is logged.

TestPostgresMigrateDriverReleasesConns checks that the schema version
calls leave no connection in use, both in the pool and on the server.
The server count is necessary because each driver uses its own handle,
which the pool stats do not include. TestPostgresMigrationSmallConnPool
runs all migrations on a fresh database with a pool of two connections,
under a one minute deadline. It reproduces the startup hang from #11007.

commit.message:
blindedpath: reject blinded paths whose aggregate fees overflow

The aggregate base fee and fee rate advertised in a blinded path's payinfo
must exactly represent the policies enforced inside the path. The previous
uint32 arithmetic could wrap, valid uint32 fee rates can overflow even a
uint64 numerator, the proportional fee was clamped to math.MaxUint32 and the
base fee was narrowed with an unchecked uint32 conversion. Each of these
silently under-reports the fee the payer must add.

Make calcBlindedPathPolicies return an error, compute both aggregates with
checked multiplication and addition, and reject an aggregate that does not
fit in the invoice's uint32 fields. The error wraps errInvalidBlindedPath,
so BuildBlindedPaymentPaths skips only that candidate, logs why, and still
builds blinded paths from the remaining usable routes.

commit.message:
scripts: add command to lint submodules

Add make lint-module to lint every non-tools Go submodule, or a single module selected with module=<path>.

Reuse the standard Docker cache and Git worktree mounts, preserve nested module paths, forward worker limits, and report all failing modules after the complete pass. The command remains opt-in and is not added to CI yet.

commit.message:
bolt12: drop the unused strict features encoder

The strict features record only ever decodes. Encode goes through
lnwire's features record, so strictFeaturesEncoder never ran and
duplicated lnwire's encoding. The record now passes its encode side
through to lnwire's record, leaving one definition of the writer and the
minimality check where it matters, on decode.

That makes minimal output on encode an lnwire property we rely on, so a
test pins it: every features field of an offer, invoice request and
invoice is written minimally, and the strict decoder accepts the result.

commit.message:
bolt12: follow the offer-less node id rule

For an invoice that answers a request with no offer, BOLT 12 lets the
payer reject it only if it cannot confirm invoice_node_id out of band. The
payer published that request and never addressed the payee, so it usually
has no key to compare against. ValidateInvoiceForPayment still required
one and failed on nil, which left a payer no honest argument to pass. Its
doc also named a node the payer sent to, which does not exist in this flow.

A nil expectedNodeID is now accepted for such a request. A payer that did
confirm a key passes it and gets the comparison, and a response to an offer
still requires one. TestValidateInvoiceNodeID covers all three cases.

Review: https://github.com/lightningnetwork/lnd/pull/11191#discussion_r4133985071

commit.message:
bolt12: build the lnr1 encoder on EncodeSigned

A request that answers an offer reaches its peer as raw TLV inside an onion
message. A request that answers no offer is published by its payer as an
lnr1 string instead, such as a QR code, and the payee reads that string to
answer with an invoice, so the string encoder stays.

It now delegates to EncodeSigned, as EncodeInvoiceString does, so the
signature rule lives in one place. The three tests that pinned the
encoder's refusal to emit an invalid, unsigned or badly signed request move
to EncodeSigned accordingly.

commit.message:
bolt12: un-export the encode methods

EncodeSigned is the entry point for an invoice_request and an invoice that
leave the node, and the bech32 wrappers cover the string forms, so no
caller outside this package needs a serialisation that skips the signature
check. Un-exporting encode makes the writer-side requirement a property of
the API rather than a rule a caller has to remember.

Offer follows for consistency, since EncodeOfferString covers the only form
it travels in. InvoiceError keeps its exported Encode. It is unsigned, so
there is no check to skip, and raw TLV is the only form a receiver can send
it in.
